components.text: Show why the alleged obscurity of the natural-to-moral relation creates a comparative disadvantage rather than a shared stopping point.
Establish that the rival's metaphysical costs are not matched by corresponding unexplained commitments in the theistic view.
The decisive demand is to explain why the rival's allegedly obscure natural-to-moral relation creates a comparative disadvantage.
A further demand is whether the rival ontology is uniquely more extravagant or unsupported than the theistic stopping point.
Determine whether physical causal closure itself entails that mental states are causally impotent and agency is eliminated.
The decisive demand is whether physical causal closure entails that mental states are causally impotent and agency therefore disappears.
A separate component concerns whether successive mental states eliminate an enduring accountable agent.
Explain how godless normative realism can preserve genuinely supererogatory action rather than requiring every morally best act.
Assess whether the theistic command account itself clearly permits the proposed acts to remain above obligation.
The decisive demand is whether the reasons-based account can permit genuinely supererogatory conduct rather than requiring every morally best act.
A second demand is whether decisive moral reasons generate unconditional rather than merely desire-dependent obligations.
Show whether divine commands are required as the constitutive and ultimate source of every objective moral obligation.
Explain how morally relevant nondivine facts can generate obligations rather than merely conditional moral recommendations.
The decisive demand is whether divine commands uniquely constitute duties rather than merely accompanying independently obligation-generating facts.
Explain how divine commands constitute duties for agents who neither apprehend the commands nor recognize the commander's authority.
The decisive demand is whether commands constitute universal obligations for agents who do not apprehend either their content or divine authority.
Explain what necessary normative function a divine command serves when God foreknows it will not prevent the wrongful act.
The decisive demand is what necessary normative function commands serve when God foreknows that issuing them will not prevent the wrongful act.
Explain how promises, circumstances, and other morally relevant facts fit if divine commands remain the ultimate source of duty.
The decisive demand is whether promises, suffering, and circumstances disprove divine commands as the ultimate source of obligation.
Explain how nonbelievers can be bound when they do not explicitly identify God as the source of the command.
The decisive demand is how divine requirements bind nonbelievers who do not identify God as the source or commander.
Identify a nonpreventive purpose for issuing general commands despite foreknown disobedience.
The decisive demand is what purpose a divine command serves when God anticipates that it will not prevent the forbidden act.
Explain why naturalism and unguided evolution do not defeat justified confidence in broadly reliable cognitive faculties.
The decisive demand is whether naturalism and unguided evolution defeat reasonable confidence in the reliability of evolved cognition.
A further component is whether divine supervision provides a comparatively superior reliability explanation.
Explain how God's nature can serve as the intrinsic standard of goodness rather than requiring a separate abstract standard.
Show why the theistic stopping point is a coherent paradigm rather than merely a corresponding unexplained normative relation.
The decisive demand is how God's goodness can function as a foundation rather than merely another unexplained intrinsic normative fact.
A further demand is whether divine goodness avoids the same unexplained normative stopping point alleged against godless realism.
Determine whether invoking worship-worthiness explains moral goodness or embeds an unexplained normative claim in the proposed foundation.
Assess whether the divine-nature ground avoids the same kind of basic normative stopping point attributed to godless realism.
The decisive demand is whether defining God through worship worthiness explains moral normativity without presupposing a basic normative claim.
A related demand is whether God's nature supplies a nonarbitrary moral foundation that improves explanatorily on irreducible normativity.
